item.text: {"decisions":[{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0001","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Title page, navigation elements, publication metadata. Contains no substantive information about López Obrador's economic governance, policy agenda, or economic decisions. Brief biographical identifying data (name, dates, party) is not relevant to any 5B question.","exclusion_reason":"Navigation, boilerplate, and publication metadata. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Narrative political biography covering electoral victories, party switches, video scandal, desafuero, 2006 and 2012 electoral disputes. No substantive economic policy content; characterizes AMLO's political discourse and persona rather than his economic governance agenda, budgets, or professional appointments.","exclusion_reason":"Political narrative and biographical framing. No material economic governance content for any 5B question."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Covers 2006 electoral conflict, Calderón victory, López Obrador's refusal to accept results, self-proclaimed 'president legítimo,' civil disobedience campaign, international community recognition of Calderón. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral dispute narrative and opposition mobilization. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"2012 electoral defeat to Peña Nieto, fraud allegation, legal challenge, anti-PRI opposition organizing, founding of MORENA, opposition to EPN's structural reforms (energy, education, telecommunications, labor). Mentions opposition to neoliberalism and defense of Pemex, but no analysis of actual economic governance decisions or evidence of economic management.","exclusion_reason":"Political opposition narrative, electoral dispute, party founding. No material economic governance evidence for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0006","unit-0062","unit-0063"],"explanation":"Contains the full 2018 electoral program of Juntos Haremos Historia (MORENA-PT-PES). Stated priorities include: 'austeridad republicana' to redirect public resources from current spending to investment without raising taxes; combatting poverty and elevating human development for vulnerable groups; increasing domestic gasoline production to reduce imports and prices; energy and food self-sufficiency; 'erradicating' political corruption 'giving example' from Los Pinos; and defending Mexican migrants. These directly address 5B.1 (broad-based prosperity agenda vs. rents/short-term popularity), 5B.2 (qualified professionals and operational independence), 5B.6 (budget priorities), 5B.8 (distribution of gains/burdens), 5B.9 (shock response), and 5B.10 (durability of economic trajectory). This is the primary economic governance program statement for the 2018-2024 presidency.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0062","unit-0063"],"explanation":"Describes the post-election political platform (December 2018) as 'pragmatic socialdemocracy' that 'assumes orthodox free market notions, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, and peso flotation,' combined with rejection of 'privatizing tendencies' and 'foreignization' of strategic sectors, and priority for 'national production.' Explicitly commits to pursue corruption cases against ex-presidents 'doing justice without vengeance or hatred' and 'not putting Peña Nieto in jail.' Also mentions moral conservatism on abortion and same-sex marriage. Addresses 5B.1 (rejection of neoliberal model vs. national production), 5B.3 (macroeconomic stability commitments), 5B.5 (anti-corruption promise against ex-presidents), 5B.7 (reliance on slogans vs. evidence-based correction), and 5B.10 (trajectory vs. inherited model).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Covers USMCA trade negotiations, migrant caravanas at the US-Mexico border, Trump border threats, visa offers to migrants. Foreign policy and migration context, not economic governance in the sense of 5B questions.","exclusion_reason":"Foreign policy and migration/trade context. No material content on domestic economic governance for any 5B question."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Personal biographical narrative: family background, childhood in Tabasco, 1969 brother death incident, move to Palenque, family shopkeeping, early baseball and Catholic activities. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Personal biographical narrative (childhood, family). No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"University enrollment at UNAM (1972), political activation within PRI, work with indigenous communities through INI in La Chontalpa. No economic governance content relevant to any 5B question.","exclusion_reason":"University enrollment and early political career within PRI. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Delegation at COPLAMAR (1978), indigenous publication work, agricultural programs, university teaching, marriage to Rocío Beltrán, three children. Career progression within PRI bureaucracy. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Early government career and personal family details. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"1982 campaign for Governor González Pedrero, appointment as director of CEPES, then president of Tabasco PRI (January 1983), internal party conflicts, removal in November 1983, subsequent Mexico City posting at INCO consumer protection institute. 1986 book publication on Tabasco history. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Party bureaucratic career, book publication, institutional postings. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Democratic Current faction formation within PRI (1987), joining Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas in 1988 electoral coalition (FDN), Salinas election victory with alleged system collapse, López Obrador's gubernatorial defeat in Tabasco amid fraud allegations. Foundation of PRD in May 1989. Political party history, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Party political history, faction formation, electoral disputes. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"PRD presidency in Tabasco, building local support networks, 'exodus for democracy' march (1991-1992) from Villahermosa to Mexico City Zócalo. Political mobilization and protest history. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Opposition political mobilization and march protest. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"1994 gubernatorial election in Tabasco, loss to Roberto Madrazo (38.7% vs 57.5%), fraud allegations, civil resistance campaign, National Democratic Alliance creation, opposition to Salinas's Pemex segmentation. Protest and opposition history. No substantive evidence of economic governance decisions.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral protest and opposition history. No material evidence of economic governance decisions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"1996 PRD party presidency election (73.9% of votes), leftist reputation, party electoral disasters under Muñoz Ledo leadership, contrast with PAN's four gubernatorial wins. Political party leadership narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Party leadership election and internal PRD politics. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"July 1997 Mexico City mayoral election (Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas victory), PRD legislative gains, PRD party presidency handoff (April 1999) following chaotic internal election. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Party leadership transition and electoral victories of allies. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Cárdenas resignation from Mexico City mayoralty (September 1999), López Obrador's candidacy, FOBAPROA investigation publication. Mentions FOBAPROA as 'the biggest fraud in history after the Conquest' but this is a campaign document, not evidence of economic governance performance.","exclusion_reason":"FOBAPROA criticism is opposition campaign narrative, not evidence of economic governance during presidential term."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"November 1999 PRD primary for Mexico City mayoralty (75.5% victory), July 2000 federal elections where Fox defeated Labastida, López Obrador won Mexico City mayoralty with 34.5% vs Santiago Creel's 33.4%. Electoral narrative, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral results narrative. No evidence of economic governance decisions or policy execution."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Personal family tragedies (father, mother, wife deaths in 2000-2003), characterization of López Obrador's political style as charismatic, pugnacious, tenacious, nicknamed 'El Peje.' Political image and personal narrative, not governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Personal biography, family tragedies, political characterizations. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"López Obrador's oratorical style, 'mañaneras' press conferences at 6am, media strategy, political image among supporters. No substantive economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Political communication style and media strategy. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0006","unit-0063"],"explanation":"Reports specific governance outcomes of the 2000-2005 Mexico City administration: vigorous public works campaign for urban infrastructure improvement and expansion; social protection programs including the Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores (Universal Food Pension for Elderly); refusal to implement Seguro Popular citing existing free municipal coverage. Also notes PAN opposition criticism that the administration was 'populist' and overspent without concern for debt. This provides evidence on 5B.6 (budget execution producing infrastructure and social programs vs. patronage projects), 5B.8 (distribution of benefits to elderly), and 5B.7 (accountability and transparency claims).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Video scandal of March 2004: Televisa broadcast clandestine videos of PRD officials (Gustavo Ponce, René Bejarano, Carlos Ímaz) engaged in corruption—casino gambling, negotiating political favors, cash transfers in briefcases. Argentine-Mexican businessman Carlos Ahumada as central figure. This is a scandal narrative about corruption allegations against close associates, not evidence of economic governance policy or its administration.","exclusion_reason":"Scandal narrative involving associates' corruption. Not evidence of López Obrador's economic governance decisions or policies."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"López Obrador's response to the video scandal: late and tepid rejection of corrupt practices, emphasis on political conspiracy theory attributing scandal to Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and Fox. No substantive discussion of economic governance reforms or policies.","exclusion_reason":"Political response to scandal and conspiracy allegations. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"PGR request for desafuero (congressional removal of immunity) on May 18, 2004, related to a minor land expropriation case in Cuajimalpa from 2000, involving a private hospital access road. Legal/constitutional conflict narrative. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Legal/desafuero controversy over land expropriation. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"200,000 PRD supporters demonstrated in the Zócalo in August 2004 in support of López Obrador. October 2004 book 'Un proyecto alternativo de nación.' November 2004: President Fox dismissed Mexico City Public Security Secretary Marcelo Ebrard. Political mobilization and book publication, not governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Political mobilization demonstration and administrative conflict. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"April 2005 Chamber of Deputies vote (360-127) approving desafuero request. Massive civil resistance mobilization by López Obrador. Constitutional conflict between Mexico City Assembly and federal government over Supreme Court jurisdiction. Legal/constitutional narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Desafuero legal battle and congressional voting. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"May 2005 PGR fails to get judge to initiate proceedings. Fox accepts prosecutor Macedo de la Concha's resignation. April 25 civil resistance demonstration. April 27 Fox announces López Obrador can compete in elections. May 4 new prosecutor Cabeza de Vaca drops charges. Political resolution narrative of the desafuero crisis. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Resolution of desafuero legal crisis. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"July 29, 2005 López Obrador requests leave from Mexico City mayoralty to focus on PRD primary. Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas declines to compete. September 19, 2005 designated as presidential candidate of the Por el Bien de Todos coalition. December 10 oath as coalition candidate. Political candidacy narrative, not governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Presidential candidacy announcement and coalition formation. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"2006 presidential campaign narrative: Calderón's 'FeCal' nickname, López Obrador's accusations of nepotism and abuse against Calderón as BANOBRAS director and Energy secretary, class dynamics of voter preferences. Campaign political narrative, not substantive economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Campaign political attacks and electoral positioning. No substantive economic governance policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0006","unit-0046"],"explanation":"Campaign program content: ending 'privilege, corruption, and looting' starting 'from top to bottom'; reducing presidential salary by half; combatting tax fraud and evasion; austerity in government; investigating FOBAPROA via Truth Commission. Post-election economic commitments are included here: PRD would promote social development programs, extend public services to degraded areas, attend to elderly, unemployed, single mothers; agricultural, tourism, public works sectors. Rejects any privatization of Pemex. These directly address 5B.1 (ending rents/corruption vs. broad-based governance), 5B.3 (fiscal rules), 5B.4 (competitive framework), 5B.5 (anti-corruption enforcement), 5B.7 (accountability mechanisms), and 5B.10 (trajectory alternative).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Continuation of 2006 campaign program: savings from austerity (100,000 million pesos in first year), more effective tax collection as new revenue source, social program expansion, right to 'fair' and 'dignified' minimum wage, opposition to NAFTA agricultural terms, priority on migration (no wall, no militarization). Campaign promises, not evidence of actual economic governance performance.","exclusion_reason":"2006 campaign platform promises. No evidence of implemented economic governance during presidential term (which did not occur)."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"López Obrador's distancing from Chávez and Venezuela, denial of personal or institutional connections, criticism of bolívarian model. Campaign foreign policy positioning. No substantive economic governance content for any 5B question.","exclusion_reason":"Campaign foreign policy positioning and Venezuela comparisons. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"July 2006 election-night narrative: exit polls, PREP results showing Calderón's 0.64% lead, López Obrador's claim of different data showing his victory. Electoral dispute narrative, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"2006 election night dispute narrative. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"International electoral monitoring missions (OAS, EU, UN) confirm election cleanliness. López Obrador's continued protests, July 16 call for national 'peaceful civil resistance' including road blockades. Electoral opposition mobilization, not governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Post-election protests and civil resistance calls. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0035","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"TEPJF August 5 decision to order partial recount (9% of polling stations), López Obrador's rejection, August 15 call invoking Article 39 of Constitution for people to 'end the simulated Republic.' Electoral dispute and constitutional confrontation narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral tribunal proceedings and constitutional confrontation. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0036","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"TEPJF September 5 validates Calderón election. López Obrador's 'al diablo con sus instituciones' statement. September 16 National Democratic Convention (CND) called, 'legitimate government' with 12 secretaries announced. November 20 'legitimate president' ceremony in Zócalo. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Opposition 'legitimate presidency' mobilization. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0037","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"October 2006 second marriage to Beatriz Gutiérrez Müller, son Jesús Ernesto born April 2007. Personal/family content. No economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Personal family event. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0038","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"December 1, 2006 Calderón inauguration chaos, PRD legislators' disruption, Zócalo counter-demonstration, 'traitor' and 'spurious' characterizations. López Obrador book 'La mafia nos robó la Presidencia' (July 2007). Opposition political narrative, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Opposition inauguration protest and opposition book publication. No economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0039","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"2007-2008 continued opposition activities, November 2007 Mandoki film 'Fraude: México 2006,' international documentary on electoral fraud. Opposition strategy losing momentum, no government recognition. Political opposition narrative, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Continued opposition mobilization and documentary.
